documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

54F transferring care after her longtime PCP retired. Brought her bottles.

Scleroderma, limited type (CREST), diagnosed around 2016 by rheumatology. Fingers blanch in cold and with stress - has had that for years before the SSc diagnosis. Wears gloves Oct-April, amlodipine helps. Rheum keeps her on mycophenolate 1000 bid, labs through their office every few months, sees them once a year in the fall. Reflux for years, omeprazole 40 every morning, no heartburn breaking through on it. Swallowing fine. No SOB, no cough, walks the dog most evenings without trouble.

PSH: lap chole 2010. R carpal tunnel release this June, healed, numbness gone.
Meds: omeprazole 40 daily, amlodipine 5 daily, mycophenolate 1000 bid (rheum), ASA 81 daily - not sure who started the aspirin or why, has just always been on it.
All: NKDA
FH: mother RA, father HTN, sister Hashimoto.
SH: married, admin assistant at a school district office. Never smoked. Wine once or twice a month.

Exam: well appearing. Skin tightening over the fingers distal to the MCPs, no digital ulcers, nailfolds unremarkable to the eye. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear, no crackles at the bases. Abd soft, healed lap scars. No edema. R palm scar well healed.

A/P
1. Limited cutaneous SSc - per rheum, continue MMF. Will ask them to cc us on letters.
2. Raynaud - stable on amlodipine 5.
3. GERD - controlled, continue omeprazole.
4. HM: prior records requested (she thinks colonoscopy 2019 was clean, Pap 2018). Mammogram ordered. Labs today incl A1c, TSH, one-time HCV/HIV. Flu and shingles vaccine at a nurse visit next month - recombinant zoster is fine on MMF.

RTC 6 mo.

Outside rheumatology practice
Date of visit: 11/17/2022

Dear Colleague,

Thank you for taking over Mrs. Cummings's primary care. I saw her for her yearly review of limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis.

She is doing well. Raynaud attacks are typical for her for the season and manageable with gloves, hand warmers and amlodipine. No digital ulcers. Reflux is controlled. She denies dyspnea, cough or dysphagia.

Examination: BP and pulse normal. Sclerodactyly limited to the fingers, unchanged from last year; no pitting scars or ulcers. Lungs clear. Heart sounds normal.

Monitoring labs today: CBC and comprehensive panel within normal limits.

Impression: limited cutaneous SSc, stable.
Plan: continue mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg twice daily (we will continue to prescribe and monitor every 3 months). Continue amlodipine 5 mg. Return in one year.

Medications: mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg BID, amlodipine 5 mg daily, omeprazole 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Sincerely,
Rheumatology

documents.title: Office visit - chest discomfort
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: chest squeezing, see portal msg 7/19.

HPI: 56F with limited SSc. About 3-4 weeks of brief episodes of tight, squeezing discomfort behind the sternum, lasting a few minutes. Most with eating, a couple at rest at work. Never with exertion - walked 2 miles Sunday without anything. Doesn't travel. Sometimes the bite of food feels hung up mid-chest. No heartburn on her omeprazole, no regurgitation, weight steady. No dyspnea, palpitations, syncope.

Meds/allergies unchanged; NKDA.

Exam: comfortable. Vitals reviewed. Heart RRR, no murmur, rub or gallop. Lungs clear. Chest wall nontender. Abd soft, nontender. No edema.

ECG in office: NSR, normal intervals, no ST-T changes.
hs-troponin, CBC, BMP drawn.

A/P: Episodic chest pain, atypical features - pattern with meals and food sticking points toward the esophagus (SSc esophageal involvement on the list of possibilities) but she is 56 and we should exclude a cardiac cause first.
- Exercise treadmill test ordered.
- GI referral for the dysphagia.
- Continue omeprazole. ED precautions reviewed again.

documents.title: Troponin and labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your heart enzyme (troponin) was normal at 3, and the blood count and kidney tests are normal too. The stress test office will call you to schedule. Keep the GI appointment as well.

reports.text: Indication: intermittent chest discomfort. Standard Bruce protocol. Resting ECG sinus rhythm, normal. Exercised 8 minutes 30 seconds, stopped for fatigue, reaching 92% of maximum predicted heart rate. Blood pressure response normal. No chest pain during exercise or recovery. No ischemic ST segment changes. No arrhythmia.
reports.conclusion: Normal exercise treadmill test; no evidence of exercise-induced ischemia at an adequate workload.

documents.title: Gastroenterology consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology group - new consultation, 08/26/2024
Referred by: primary care, for chest discomfort and dysphagia.

Margaret Cummings is a 56-year-old woman with limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis, Raynaud phenomenon and reflux.

She describes spells of abrupt, severe pressure behind the breastbone that she calls squeezing. They last several minutes, most often come on during a meal, occasionally at rest, and are unrelated to effort. The pain stays central. Solids sometimes seem to stop partway down. A warm drink often helps. On omeprazole she has no heartburn now. No weight loss and no regurgitation.

Cardiac evaluation through her PCP: ECG normal, troponin normal, and an exercise treadmill test on 8/6 without ischemia.

PMH: limited SSc (rheumatology), Raynaud, GERD.
PSH: laparoscopic cholecystectomy; right carpal tunnel release.
Medications: omeprazole 40 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg twice daily, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: none known.
Family history: mother rheumatoid arthritis, father hypertension, sister Hashimoto thyroiditis.
Social: never smoker, wine rarely, works as an administrative assistant.

Vital signs normal. Exam unremarkable: abdomen soft and nontender, no adenopathy.

Barium esophagram performed today (separate report): weak, disordered distal peristalsis with slow emptying; no stricture or mass.

Assessment: chest pain and solid dysphagia from esophageal dysmotility, in keeping with esophageal involvement of systemic sclerosis. Cardiac causes reasonably excluded.

Plan:
1. High-resolution esophageal manometry - ordered.
2. Continue omeprazole 40 mg daily.
3. Small bites, chew well, sip warm fluids with meals, stay upright after eating.
4. Will write again with manometry results.

Gastroenterology

documents.title: Esophageal manometry results
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology group
High-resolution esophageal manometry, 09/17/2024

Ten 5 mL supine wet swallows. Upper esophageal sphincter: normal resting pressure and relaxation. Lower esophageal sphincter resting pressure 9 mmHg (low); relaxation normal. Esophageal body: 8 of 10 swallows ineffective (80%), with weak distal contractile vigor; no premature or spastic contractions; no outflow obstruction.

Impression: ineffective esophageal motility with a hypotensive lower esophageal sphincter, consistent with esophageal involvement of systemic sclerosis.

Dear colleague, this confirms the dysmotility we suspected. No medication change: continue omeprazole 40 mg daily, which matters more given the weak sphincter. She is already using the eating measures we discussed and says the spells are less frequent. GI follow-up as needed.

Gastroenterology

Outside pulmonary function laboratory
Date of test: 12/09/2025
Ordering: rheumatology. Copy to primary care.

Spirometry, lung volumes and DLCO. Good effort, acceptable and reproducible.

FVC 91% predicted
FEV1 89% predicted
FEV1/FVC 0.78

documents.title: Cardiology consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group - consultation 02/19/2026
Referred by rheumatology; copy to primary care.

Reason: worsening fatigue and breathlessness on exertion.

Ms. Cummings, 57, has limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis. She was seen by GI in August 2024 for chest pain and swallowing trouble and was found to have esophageal dysmotility. Over roughly the past twelve months she has become steadily more fatigued and more winded with exertion. She still has difficulty getting solid food down. Her fingers still go white and hurt in the cold, and the skin over her hands feels tight.

Medications: mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg twice daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, omeprazole 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily. NKDA.
Family history: mother rheumatoid arthritis, father hypertension, sister Hashimoto thyroiditis. Never smoker, rare alcohol.

Examination: the skin over the fingers is taut and shiny. Telangiectasias on the face. Heart: the pulmonic component of S2 is loud. Lungs clear. No edema.

Data reviewed: PFTs 12/2025 with preserved spirometry and volumes and DLCO reduced to 51% predicted. NT-proBNP today 410 pg/mL.

Assessment: progressive exertional dyspnea in limited SSc, with a loud P2 and an isolated low DLCO. Pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with systemic sclerosis is suspected.

Plan:
1. Transthoracic echocardiogram.
2. Right heart catheterization through our pulmonary hypertension clinic to confirm.
3. No medication changes for now.

Cardiology

reports.text: Indication: dyspnea, suspected pulmonary hypertension in systemic sclerosis. Left ventricle normal in size with normal wall thickness and systolic function; LVEF 60%. No regional wall motion abnormality. Right ventricle mildly dilated with preserved systolic function, TAPSE 18 mm. Estimated right ventricular systolic pressure 56 mmHg. Atria normal in size. Valves structurally normal. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Normal left ventricular function, LVEF 60%. Mildly dilated right ventricle with preserved function. Estimated RVSP 56 mmHg.

documents.title: Pulmonary hypertension clinic - catheterization and treatment
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group, pulmonary hypertension clinic
Visit 04/02/2026 (catheterization 03/31/2026)

Dear colleague,

Ms. Cummings underwent right heart catheterization on 3/31 via the right internal jugular vein, without complication.

Hemodynamics:
Right atrial pressure 6 mmHg
Mean pulmonary artery pressure 36 mmHg
Pulmonary artery wedge pressure 10 mmHg
Cardiac output 4.6 L/min, cardiac index 2.7 L/min/m2
Pulmonary vascular resistance 5.7 Wood units

Six-minute walk on 4/2: 405 m, lowest SpO2 94%.

Together with her echo (estimated RVSP 56 mmHg, mildly dilated RV with preserved function), NT-proBNP of 410 and the isolated low DLCO, this confirms precapillary pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with systemic sclerosis.

Plan, discussed at length with her:
1. Upfront combination therapy: ambrisentan 5 mg daily and tadalafil 20 mg daily, starting 4/2/2026. Tadalafil will go up to 40 mg daily after four weeks if tolerated. Both through a specialty pharmacy, prescribed by our clinic.
2. Continue her other medications, including mycophenolate per rheumatology.
3. Return in about 3 months with a six-minute walk and NT-proBNP.

Medications after this visit: ambrisentan 5 mg daily, tadalafil 20 mg daily, mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg BID, amlodipine 5 mg daily, omeprazole 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily. NKDA.

Pulmonary Hypertension Clinic
